solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sleeping quarters of Everest climbers maybe greatly affected?

definitions.text: Sleeping quarters of Everest climbers maybe
definitions.meaning: a tented base set up far up the mountain, where climbers rest before the summit push
exaggerated and theatrical in manner, ostentatiously over the top

explanation.surface: A wry question whether mountaineers' tents are terribly showy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a camp pitched at altitude. The second is the idiom for flamboyant, exaggerated theatricality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed phrases: a camp at altitude on a mountain, and the idiom for extravagantly theatrical style.

clue.text: Suffers heavy blow? Cushion needed

parts.note: to have an illness is to suffer it, as in has flu
a sock is a hard punch

explanation.surface: Someone takes a thump and needs something soft to land on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a thick firm cushion for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: Smile: daughter is to prepare the coffee?

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A cheerful parent says their daughter must make the coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: grinding beans is one way to prepare coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are ground before brewing, so crushing them is a step in making the drink.

clue.text: Mechanic has repaired ATM

indicators.note: repaired means fixed up, reassembled, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A technician fixes a broken bank machine.
explanation.definitionFit: ATM stands for automated teller machine, the device dispensing banknotes from a bank account.

clue.text: Fellow injured in a scrum

indicators.note: injured means damaged or hurt, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man gets hurt in a rugby scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum is the rugby set piece where packed forwards push against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus is a man's name, and in crosswords any male first name can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: Dog exercises round eastern parts of Hyde Park

indicators.note: the exercise letters go around the picked letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises

indicators.note: on a map east is to the right, so the right-hand ends of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A dog being walked in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern parts of' takes E and K, the right-hand ends of Hyde and Park; 'round' puts PE around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Peke is the short familiar name for a Pekingese, a small breed of toy dog.

clue.text: Record one lightweight remark that's witty

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is a kind of record
I is the Roman numeral one
a gram is a tiny unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone records a single throwaway quip that turns out to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short pithy saying, typically clever and pointed.

clue.text: Finish piece of satire, ignoring introduction

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for satire is left off

parts.note: a send-up is a parody that mocks its subject

explanation.surface: Completing a lampoon but skipping its opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is a phrasal verb meaning to finish or land somewhere eventually.

clue.text: European vessel going round Western Isles

indicators.note: the ship's letters surround the others, as a vessel circles islands

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes a vessel's name
IS is an abbreviation for islands or isles

explanation.surface: A continental ship sailing around Scotland's Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Western Isles are the Outer Hebrides of Scotland, but here the phrase splits into W and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss person comes from Switzerland, a nation in Europe, so they are an example of a European.

clue.text: Reacted after agent provided misinformation?

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as a sales agent
to tell untruths, put in the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone responded once a spy had fed them false information.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer someone is to respond or react to what they said, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Start to pour alcoholic drink over dining room furniture, as expected?

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of pour
in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the drink is read backwards

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink of fermented apples
a table is the main furniture of a dining room

explanation.surface: Someone pours a drink over the dinner table, as you might have guessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses CIDER to REDIC. The definition loosely stands for an adjective: an outcome as expected is foreseeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens as expected was foreseeable, so it is easily foretold.

clue.text: Unusual old doctor of religion

parts.note: O is a common abbreviation for old; the answer's letters also run backwards across old doctor, a coincidence
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a degree in theology

explanation.surface: An elderly theologian who is rather peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or out of the ordinary is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Cheap cheese initially appetising: puts more out

indicators.note: out as in wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
takes the opening letter of appetising

explanation.surface: Bargain cheese looks tempting, so a shopkeeper displays more of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A from appetising; 'out' rearranges A with PUTSMORE. The definition is jocular: cheap cheese is what you bait the device with.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap cheese is a joking description of the trap, since the bait it holds is a cheap bit of cheese.

clue.text: Before school, Christopher shows lack of good taste

indicators.note: the name's letters come before the abbreviation for school

parts.note: Kit is a common short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A boy reveals vulgar preferences even before starting school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art or decor that is gaudy and tasteless, so it embodies an absence of refinement.

clue.text: More tart and port

definitions.meaning: sharper or more sour in flavour
a harbour city in northern Morocco facing the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: A sharper flavour, and a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the fortified wine, matching 'tart' as a taste; it is the Moroccan harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangy means sharply flavoured, so the comparative is sharper; the other sense is the Moroccan seaport.

clue.text: More secure business with monarch

parts.note: a firm is a business company
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A company gains stability by attaching itself to royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means stable or fixed, so the comparative means steadier or more secure.

clue.text: Read law about unfair treatment

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to study legal texts about being treated unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is an idiom for harsh or unjust handling.

clue.text: Guide people over hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits above the second

parts.note: men stands for people in general
a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A leader takes a group across a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted adviser who guides a less experienced person.

clue.text: Happy to tour one northern land-mass

indicators.note: the word for happy goes around the others, as a tourist goes round a place

parts.note: content means satisfied or happy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cheerful traveller sets out to see a large northern territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is one of the earth's great land-masses, such as Asia or Africa.

clue.text: What's topping cake — really extravagant and mouth-watering?

definitions.text: What's topping cake — really extravagant and mouth-watering?

indicators.note: in a down clue the tops of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Asking what goes on a cake that is indulgent and delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' takes the first letters of cake, really, extravagant, and, mouth-watering; the whole clue also describes the dairy topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped dairy topping is spread or piped on a cake, rich and luscious.

clue.text: Chop some of the wood

indicators.note: only part of the letters of these words is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut up some of the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to cut or chop with an axe, the plain synonym.

clue.text: Run in preliminary contest, showing courage

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for preliminary contest

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete shows bravery while running a qualifying race.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart can mean bravery or spirit, as in losing heart.

clue.text: Distinguished English conservation group protecting underground tunnel

indicators.note: the English letter and the charity's letters surround the tunnel, as if guarding it

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the UK heritage conservation charity
a mine is a tunnel dug underground

explanation.surface: An English heritage body safeguards an old subterranean passage.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that preserves historic buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent and distinguished are synonyms for someone celebrated and highly regarded.

clue.text: Fire beginning to burn at front of lounge

indicators.note: the picked letter is placed ahead of the word for lounge
takes the opening letter of burn

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: A fire starts to burn at the front of a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A blaze is a large, fiercely burning fire, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Cause harm to small planet

parts.note: to mar something is to damage or spoil it
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Doing damage to a minor world.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fourth world from the sun, an example of a planet in our solar system.

clue.text: Relation dispatched from the east

indicators.note: dispatched as in killed off or broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family member has been sent over from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' looks like part of the surface story of travel, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things of or originating in the countries of Asia.
